storylines.name: The Iran war with no exit strategy and the Strait of Hormuz still choked
storylines.note: winnable if anyone meant it, but Trump wavers between hoping sanctions topple the regime and declaring victory and leaving, while Iran rearms and oil and diesel stay disrupted

storylines.name: The $40 trillion debt showing up in long-term bond yields
storylines.note: markets are pricing in default or inflation, only spending cuts fix it, and Bessent's buybacks and yield-curve tricks are central planning that touches nothing real

storylines.name: Trump's tariff war on Canada and China
storylines.note: a tax Americans pay that has failed every stated goal, and Canada should go to zero unilaterally instead of retaliating

storylines.name: Israel after October 7: Gaza stalemate, Turkey, and being undercut by Washington
storylines.note: Hamas will never disarm so Israel should not withdraw first, Turkey is becoming the bigger flashpoint than Iran, and Israel is held to a standard Russia and Iran never are

storylines.name: US military decline under Hegseth: Navy catapults, drone units, empty munitions stocks
storylines.note: self-inflicted erosion by unqualified appointees reverting to 'basics' while ignoring the drone and AI lessons of Ukraine and Israel

storylines.name: Russia grinding down Ukraine while its own state rots
storylines.note: Ukraine is defenseless without Patriots, Russia jails dissenters and fires the economists who warn about the war economy, and Trump calls Putin an ally

storylines.name: AI data centers turned into a bipartisan political target
storylines.note: the least wanted thing in America now, and the AI industry's own leaders fed the fear instead of making the case

storylines.name: Trump turning state power on critics, media and elections
storylines.note: FCC license threats, a DOJ run by his former defense lawyer, a mail-ballot order the courts blocked, and selling early access to market-moving posts

storylines.name: Open antisemitism and racial tribalism moving onto the right
storylines.note: the mirror image of left identity politics he says he predicted in 2015, now in Tucker's Shapiro monologue, campus chants and Republican primary votes

storylines.name: DSA-aligned socialists winning Democratic nominations
storylines.note: more honest than mainstream Democrats about abolishing capitalism, closer to East Germany than Scandinavia, and Mamdani's rent freeze is already raising rents

storylines.name: Trump courting dictators while treating allies as adversaries
storylines.note: Kim, Putin and a Venezuela oil deal on one side, Canada, South Korea, Europe and Israel on the other, which he calls the worst-performing part of the administration

storylines.name: Government equity stakes in private companies
storylines.note: roughly thirty deals and $30 billion of ownership done without a congressional vote, industrial policy dressed as privatization, and a tool the next Democrats will use for ESG

storylines.name: JD Vance's mysticism as a disqualification file
storylines.note: he is deliberately collecting the clips about dark energy, providence and the Antichrist to preempt any lesser-evil case for voting for him

themes.name: The Trump administration
themes.angle: judged on results and on economic literacy, not on which team it is on

themes.name: Capitalism versus the mixed economy
themes.angle: we have never had capitalism, so the problems people blame on markets are the government's

themes.name: Government intervention as cronyism and central planning
themes.angle: tariffs, subsidies, equity stakes and liability threats serve pressure groups, never a principle

themes.name: Human achievement and technology, AI above all
themes.angle: presumptively good, worth awe, and opposition to it is fear that has not earned itself

themes.name: Tribalism and indifference to truth on left and right
themes.angle: woke never went away, it changed target, and the same anti-truth epistemology now runs the right

themes.name: Israel, antisemitism and the double standard
themes.angle: criticism of Israel is measured against how Russia and Iran are treated for the same acts

themes.name: Altruism versus rational self-interest
themes.angle: the moral premise a culture accepts is what finally explains its foreign policy and its politics

themes.name: Individual and parental responsibility instead of corporate liability
themes.angle: a product is only blameworthy when it uses force or fraud, never when people choose to overuse it

themes.name: Islamic totalitarianism and the refusal to name the enemy
themes.angle: twenty-five years of not naming it is why 1979, 9/11, Gaza and the current war are one story

themes.name: Immigration, especially the high-skilled kind
themes.angle: immigrants founded the companies, so restricting legal immigration is self-harm, not protection

themes.name: Free speech, cancellation and the sanction of evil
themes.angle: he is not against cancelling, only against cancelling for unjust or trivial reasons

themes.name: Art, culture and Objectivism
themes.angle: he judges a work by whether reason and human agency drive it, and notes how completely Rand is left out of serious treatments of capitalism.

themes.name: Free trade
themes.angle: a tariff is a tax paid at home, and unilateral free trade benefits whoever adopts it no matter what the other side does.

themes.name: Ideas drive history
themes.angle: Marx is the unacknowledged foundation of almost all talk about capitalism, and bad philosophy travels from journals to podcasts to policy.

themes.name: Nobody is defending capitalism
themes.angle: the DSA left and the Vance/Tucker right are both statist, so the moral case for markets goes unmade on every platform that matters.

themes.name: Spending, entitlements and the fiscal arithmetic
themes.angle: the deficit is a spending problem, taxes cannot close it, and the gerontocracy transfers wealth from the young because old people vote.

themes.name: Art and aesthetics
themes.angle: judge a work on its own terms and by whether reason is the source of the hero's power, not by fidelity or casting rows

themes.name: Debt, deficits, inflation and the Fed
themes.angle: spending is the disease, price rises from supply shocks are not monetary inflation, and stagnation is the likeliest ending

themes.name: Defending capitalism against its critics
themes.angle: the critics never define the word, they leave the entrepreneur out of the picture, and Marx's exploitation story still sits under nearly all of it

themes.name: Technology and AI as human progress
themes.angle: presumptively good and worth defending out loud; the fear is unearned and deregulation, not permission, is the answer

themes.name: The human achievement roundup
themes.angle: rockets, mRNA vaccines, drones and falling battery prices as the standing evidence that free people and markets deliver

themes.name: Tribalism and the crisis of reason on both left and right
themes.angle: woke never left, it changed targets; the vice is caring about loyalty rather than truth, and the right has it too

moves.main: trace the problem to the specific government policy that caused it instead of letting it be blamed on markets in general
secondary: economic power is a trade you can walk away from; political power is the gun
hold a politician to his own stated goal and show every action contradicts it
no collectivizing blame or credit onto a group, a nationality or a company's employees
engaging with or excusing a bad actor is itself a sanction that empowers him
count the unseen cost, not just the visible gain the government points at
judge a leader by whether there is long-term strategy behind the move or only personality
any account of capitalism that leaves out the entrepreneur is broken before it starts
do the arithmetic first: show a program is unaffordable before arguing it is also immoral
prices carry real information, and a planner overriding them is not smarter than the market
define the term before arguing about it, especially 'capitalism'
treat an official justification as a claim to verify, not as a reason
mysticism in a ruler is pre-Enlightenment and disqualifying, whatever else he gets right
